# Hollow single-cell geometry: connected faces need not glue at parity cost

This is an exact structural obstruction, not an OC counterexample. In
particular, its atomic measure has a direct occupied-parity centerpoint;
see `candidate 237f4727836ebab9`.
The obstruction applies to positive decompositions into lifts over the
ORIGINAL base. A canonical integer graph lift avoids that restriction.

## 1. Audit of the two slice-lift sources

The proofs in
`candidate 185fb6155f830e0e`
and
`candidate 0798d34d2fb14df0`
pass as their stated conditional structural theorems. In particular:

* Common scalar normalization preserves joint Brunn--Minkowski at every
  integer-output convex combination, including after simultaneous weak
  limits. The compact-neighborhood Portmanteau argument has the right signs.
* Homothetic measure domination is a measure inequality, not merely support
  inclusion. Absolute continuity in the intrinsic output dimension then
  forces equality of input/output dimensions and tangent spaces.
* An interior integer base identifies the full vertical affine kernel.
  This correctly supplies the single affine perpendicular graph needed by
  an ordinary lift over the original base.
* The optimized unequal-radius-ball inequality gives the residual density
  exponent N-q. Its bounded upper-semicontinuous extension and the ball
  lift preserve the entire measure and all ambient halfspaces.
* Hollow maximal-face lifts form a cover, not a partition. Neither source
  claims a total parity budget for allocating their intersections.

One harmless notation clarification: the residual-power proof initially
writes f_epsilon on the relative interior, while its Fubini integral is
on the whole affine hull. The same displayed ball-average formula extends
f_epsilon to that hull; with this extension the equality is exact.
Simultaneous finite limits, the positive-rate rank drop, and compatibility
with an existing critical cap law remain hypotheses, as the sources say.

## 2. A twelve-point hollow projection

Use base coordinates (x,y,z), write e_i for the coordinate unit vectors,
and set r=(2,1,1). Let

    B=conv{0,2e_1,2e_2,2e_3,r}.

Its exact inequality description is

    x,y,z>=0,  y+z<=2,  x+y-z<=2,  x-y+z<=2.                 (1)

Every interior lattice point would have y,z>=1 and y+z<2, an
impossibility. Thus B is hollow. Its complete integer set is

    P=(2 Delta_3 intersect Z^3) union {a,r},  a=(1,1,1),     (2)

where 2 Delta_3={x,y,z>=0:x+y+z<=2}. In particular |P|=12.
All eight parities occur. The parity-000 points are
0,2e_1,2e_2,2e_3; parity 011 contains (0,1,1) and r.

Define b=0 on 2 Delta_3 intersect Z^3, b(a)=1/2, and b(r)=1.
The convex set

    D=conv{(0,0),(2e_1,0),(2e_2,0),(2e_3,0),(r,1)}
       subset R^3 x R

has EXACTLY the singleton fiber {b(p)} at every p in P.
Here is a direct proof that also proves (1)-(2). Let t be the convex
coefficient of r in a representation of a base p=(x,y,z). The other
four coefficients are

    lambda_1=x/2-t, lambda_2=y/2-t/2, lambda_3=z/2-t/2,
    lambda_0=1-(x+y+z)/2+t.

They are all nonnegative exactly when

    max{0,(x+y+z-2)/2} <= t <= min{x/2,y,z}.                 (3)

Nonemptiness of this interval is equivalent to (1). For the ten old
integer points the interval is {0}; for a it is {1/2}; for r it is {1}.
Enumerating x,y,z in {0,1,2} gives precisely (2). The lifted physical
height equals t, proving the singleton assertion.

The graph b is not globally affine: its values at the affine basis
0,2e_1,2e_2,2e_3 force an affine extension to be zero, but b(r)=1.
At real base (1/2,1/2,1/2), (3) is [0,1/4]; hence D has vertical
thickness away from the sampled integer bases.

## 3. The maximal occupied faces are connected

Call a face occupied if its relative interior contains an integer point.
The maximal occupied faces of B are the triangle

    F=conv{2e_2,2e_3,r}={y+z=2} intersect B

and the five edges

    [0,2e_1], [0,2e_2], [0,2e_3], [2e_1,2e_2], [2e_1,2e_3]. (4)

The triangle F has the five integer points 2e_2,2e_3,(0,1,1),a,r;
a is in its relative interior. Each listed edge has an integer midpoint.
For verification, the other five facets lie on x=0, y=0, z=0,
x+y-z=2, and x-y+z=2. None has an interior integer point: respectively
use two positive integer coordinates with sum<2, or, on either last
facet, the strict inequality y+z<2 with y,z>0. The remaining three
edges incident with r are primitive, and the old edge [2e_2,2e_3]
is contained in F. All vertices belong to the listed occupied faces.
This proves maximality and exhaustion.

These six faces form a connected overlap graph. The five edges are
connected through 0 and 2e_1, and F meets them at 2e_2 and 2e_3.
The restrictions are affine: b=x/2 on F and b=0 on every listed edge.
Thus even connected overlapping liftable face pieces do not force one
affine physical graph over the original base.

## 4. Actual single-global-cell positive-rate slices realize the example

Take ambient continuous dimension d=2 and sliced dimension N=1. Embed D
as x_2=0, using x_1 for its last coordinate. For integers j>=12 put

    epsilon_j=1/(12j),
    D_j=D+{(0_base,s,t): |s|<=epsilon_j, 0<=t<=epsilon_j}.

These are full-dimensional convex bodies in R^3 x R^2 in one common
compact set. Their exact integer fibers are the rectangles

    [b(p)-epsilon_j,b(p)+epsilon_j] x [0,epsilon_j].

Their total mixed 2-volume is M_j=24 epsilon_j^2=1/(6j^2).
Use ONE global affine function and ONE common rate:

    A_j(p,x_1,x_2)=x_2+exp(-2j)>0, lambda_j=j, s_j=exp(-j).

The level A_j=s_j is strictly inside every rectangle. Indeed exp(j)>12j
for j>=12 (the cubic term of its exponential series already suffices).
Its continuous gradient has norm one. The required inverse-volume coarea
normalization is exactly

    alpha_j=1/(M_j lambda_j |c_j|)=6j=1/(2epsilon_j).

Every normalized one-dimensional slice has mass one and converges to

    mu_p=delta_(b(p),0).

Thus the example satisfies the common normalization, simultaneous finite
limits, full global convex cell, and rank drop q=0<N=1 of the two audited
sources. It is not asserted to satisfy all canonical minimizing or critical
cap conditions. At every integer-output convex combination, singleton
support compatibility and equal masses give the joint N=1 measure
Brunn--Minkowski inequality directly.

## 5. Positive lift allocation over the original base costs at least nine

Here is the exact allocation class. Decompose mu=sum_(p in P)
 delta_(p,b(p)) into finitely many positive measures mu_i. Every nonzero
mu_i is the pushforward of mixed ordinary volume of a convex body with
positive full-dimensional auxiliary continuous fibers at its positive
bases, under ONE affine map preserving the original base p. Let k_i be
the number of parities occupied by its positive bases. Different pieces
may have different auxiliary dimensions, and fractional allocations of
any source atom are allowed. Zero-dimensional auxiliary fibers also fit,
with the same affine-graph conclusion below.

Then

    sum_i k_i >=9 > 2^3.                                   (5)

An affine base-preserving map has physical component B_i p+L_i u+b_i.
On any positive full-dimensional fiber its image is supported on the
single allowed source atom. Consequently L_i=0: a nonzero linear map
cannot be constant almost everywhere on a full-dimensional convex body.
Thus the atom heights within every piece agree with one affine function
of the original base.

If sum_i k_i<=8, each of the eight source parities appears in exactly
one piece. The four parity-000 atoms must therefore all appear with
positive mass in a single piece. Convexity and Brunn--Minkowski force
that piece to have positive volume at (0,1,1), the midpoint of 2e_2
and 2e_3. That piece occupies parity 011, so it must also contain the
positive atom at r. Its affine physical height is zero at the four
affinely independent old vertices, hence zero at r, contradicting
b(r)=1. This proves (5), including fractional allocations and pieces
not restricted to the maximal occupied faces.

The occupied-parity cost nine is attained by an exact partition:

* all five atoms on F, with physical height x/2 (three parities);
* the three atoms on [0,2e_1], with height zero (two parities);
* four singleton pieces at e_2,e_3,e_1+e_2,e_1+e_3 (one each).

Each piece is lattice-complete in its own convex hull. The product of
that hull with an auxiliary unit interval, projected by the stated
height graph, supplies an ordinary lift with the desired unit weights.
The total cost is 3+2+4=9. This is the generous occupied-parity price;
the coarser price 2^(affine base dimension) is 4+2+4=10 here.

## 6. Scope and the correct escape

There is no contradiction with a direct atomic centerpoint: the actual
lifted graph retains every same-parity geometric midpoint. A finite
colored midpoint theorem gives depth at least total mass/8 immediately.
For a concrete check, the atom over e_1 is the midpoint of the atoms
over 0 and 2e_1, so every containing closed halfspace has mass at least
two. The cap x-3(y+z)>=1 contains exactly e_1 and 2e_1. Its depth is
therefore exactly 2, or 1/6 of total mass, already above 1/8.
Nor does (5) rule out a canonical lift of the INTEGER base: such a lift
can raise its rank while retaining its exact eight occupied parities.
The obstruction is specifically to a positive decomposition into ordinary
uniform lifts over the original base with total occupied-parity cost eight.
It does not justify stopping a direct stratified centerpoint approach.

The exact arithmetic verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_hollow_single_cell_nine_parity_obstruction_independent.py`.
